summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for generalized weakness and feeling unwell, with concern for a possible urinary tract infection due to his chronic indwelling Foley catheter. He had no fever, chills, or laboratory signs of infection. Blood work was unremarkable, and urine culture grew Serratia marcescens and Enterococcus, but these were considered colonizers rather than active infection. His catheter was changed, and he reported feeling much better the following morning. Weakness was likely due to mild dehydration, possibly exacerbated by high iced tea intake and heat exposure. He was discharged home with services, with adjustments to his medications including a reduced dose of citalopram and addition of docusate for constipation. Follow-up was advised with urology for routine catheter care and monitoring of a stable right renal mass.
